ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark grey). High-intensity (white) pixels are localized and represent approximately 5-8% of the visible fluke area, primarily at the distal left tip and scattered as individual point-clusters.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Uniform dark-field pigmentation across the main body of both lobes. Significant high-contrast contiguous cluster (white/beige) at the distal tip of the left lobe. Discrete high-intensity point-clusters (white dots) scattered across the ventral surface, particularly concentrated in the lower-central region.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Distinct V-shaped notch with a calculated convergence angle of approximately 65 degrees and a bounding-box depth approximately 1/6th of the vertical fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Left lobe trailing edge exhibits high-amplitude, irregular indentations and peaks. Right lobe trailing edge exhibits a more consistent, lower-amplitude serration pattern with smaller, higher-frequency peaks.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave trajectory from the median notch to the distal tips, creating a tapered wing-like profile.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Heavy cluster of circular/rosette-shaped high-contrast pixel groups concentrated at the distal edge of the left lobe. Randomly distributed, individual high-contrast circular spots (potential barnacles or scars) are visible across the central pigmentation of both lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Localized trauma or heavy epibiotic colonization on the left fluke tip, resulting in significant textural irregularity and high-contrast pigmentation change compared to the right tip.
other_distinctive_markers: The left lobe distal tip has a unique jagged profile with a specific indentation likely caused by the high-density barnacle cluster.
